thread:
alex: Heads up — the console shows a big p95 jump for /v1/generate in eu-west, but sample counts are tiny. Anyone else seeing a mismatch between per-endpoint and aggregated percentiles?
sam: Yeah saw that. p50 looks fine, p95/p99 are all over the map. Could be sampling/origin tagging leak.
priya: My hunch: we're mixing merge-of-tdigests with raw-sample percentiles. The rollup API returns tdigests per origin, and the UI blends them without weighting counts.
luis: Can you paste the exact query the console issues? In the UI I see it calling the rollup percentiles endpoint.
priya: ```sql
SELECT approx_percentile(95, latency_ms) as p95, sum(count) as sample_count
FROM metrics_rollup
WHERE route = '/v1/generate' AND origin IN ('edge','cache-hit','backend')
GROUP BY window
```
alex: That's the one. The console calls /rollup/percentile?mode=merge which returns serialized tdigests per series; the legend then shows a blended p95 per label but it drops the sample_count, so small-origin tdigests can skew the visible percentiles.
sam: Right — labels like origin=cache-hit vs origin=backend have vastly different counts. Blending tdigests without weights will produce misleading percentiles.
priya: Two ways to fix: 1) server-side: compute final percentile after grouping (accurate but more CPU), or 2) client-side: send tdigest+count and do a weighted merge in the console before showing. Which is cheaper?
luis: Server-side gives a single correct number and keeps console simple. But for dashboard with many series that's expensive. Client-side needs the UI to be able to merge tdigests + counts; we already ship tdigest bytes in the payload.
alex: Can we at least expose sample_count in the time-series payload? Product has asked for a "confidence" badge before. Right now the legend hides counts.
priya: Agree — exposing sample_count is a low-friction win. It also lets us show an "approximate" badge when blends are unweighted.
deploy-bot: deploy started: console-ui@release-4.12.1 and rollup-api@canary. Will report back.
sam: Short-term mitigation: mark blended series with a tooltip: "This percentile is derived by merging origin-level rollups; counts vary across origins. Use exact server-side grouping for precise p95." Also show sample_count as a tiny badge next to series.
luis: Also noticed another odd case: the per-route split shows a lower p95 than the global p95 for the same window. That's impossible unless windows or count semantics differ — likely label normalization mismatch (route vs endpoint).
priya: Correct — console groups by "endpoint" but rollups are keyed by "route". We need a mapping layer in the console to align labels when we render breakdowns.
alex: Action items: 1) add sample_count to series payload (console) — alex will own that. 2) tooltip + unweighted badge (sam). 3) add route->endpoint mapping backfill (alex). 4) spike server-side final-percentile compute and measure CPU (priya). If server-side proves fast for common windows, we can flip on an exact mode.
sam: I'll prototype the legend badge/tooltip now. Will avoid perf-heavy DOM stuff.
priya: I'll run a quick perf spike: merge tdigest per-window server-side with memoization and see CPU/mem for 1h of heavy dashboards.
luis: For repro: use this curl to hit the canary rollup API with skewed origins, it reliably reproduces the mismatch. Ping me and I'll share the synthetic generator script.
alex: Thanks team. Once deploy-bot posts success we'll validate on staging and then roll to prod. (reacts :thumbsup:)
